scenario: A 32-year-old female presents as a trauma activation after being bucked off a horse, with hypotension, GCS 8, right temporal hematoma, unstable pelvis, perineal hematoma, and FAST positive free fluid in the RUQ. The scenario focuses on airway management in a hypotensive head-injured trauma patient, pelvic fracture management, transfusion, TXA, and recognition/treatment of herniation.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Start a liter of normal saline wide open now — she's hypotensive and tachycardic.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Get me a FAST ultrasound at the bedside now — she's still shocky and I want to look for free fluid.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: FAST is back — free fluid in the RUQ, no pericardial effusion. Liter of saline is in; she's still hypotensive at 81/41, HR 122, GCS 8.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Hang 2 units of packed red cells now and activate the massive transfusion protocol — she's in hemorrhagic shock, still 81/41 after the liter of saline. Get surgery down here.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Starting massive transfusion protocol — 2 units packed RBCs going up now. I'll keep pressure bags on and monitor for transfusion reaction.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Add 2 units of plasma to the massive transfusion now — keep the ratio balanced. She's still hypotensive despite the saline and red cells.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Hanging 2 units of plasma now, running per massive transfusion ratio.
